## Simple explanation

JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is a readable text format for data. It is
widely used to send requests and responses between applications, including
applications that use AI services.

## Technical explanation

JSON represents objects as key-value pairs, arrays as ordered lists, and values
as strings, numbers, booleans, null, objects, or arrays. The format is
language-independent, although each programming language has its own parser and
data types.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Model-serving APIs commonly accept JSON inputs and return JSON outputs. JSON is
also used for configuration, metadata, evaluation results, and tool-call
arguments, so engineers need to validate its structure and handle parsing
errors.

## How it works

An application serializes in-memory data into JSON text before sending or
storing it. A receiving application parses that text and can validate the
resulting structure before using the values.

## Practical example

```json
{
  "model": "text-classifier",
  "input": "The package arrived on time.",
  "labels": ["positive", "neutral", "negative"]
}
```

An inference endpoint could use these fields to select a model, process an
input, and constrain the allowed output labels.

## Common misconceptions

- JSON is a data format, not a database or programming language.
- Valid JSON does not guarantee that the data has the fields or value types an
  application expects.
- JSON does not support comments or trailing commas in its standard syntax.
